biggestGap: The entire round-8 flesh deliverable is switched OFF on the shipping configuration: species.js gates `fleshCells` behind `pxFade(c, 3.4)`, whose own header records the coarse octave at weight 0.70 at the 640x360 review frame, and portrait renders the same cut face at 0.745x linear (frozen `foam` ellipse a 45.92 -> 34.21), which pushes fwidth past the 1/3.4 edge and takes the mesh, the groove, the 1.20 relief and the roughness redistribution with it -- so desktop gained flesh_mean_rgb R 131.0 -> 150.6 while portrait gained 93.8 -> 96.3, 13% of it, and portrait's flesh_GR went the WRONG way, 0.4917 -> 0.5060 against plate-01's 0.3505.

(1) IS THE NEW STRUCTURE RESOLVED OBJECTS? NO -- and the probe is unambiguous.
  * speck_median_area 2.0 -> 2.0. Third round with no movement. Plate at matched
    scale is 4.0, at native 6.0. Our bright flesh detail is still a 2-px spike.
  * speck_cov_pct 18.97 -> 17.62 against a matched-plate 25.24 -- the WRONG
    direction, and the same wrong direction r7 flagged (r6->r7 was 20.87 -> 18.97).
    Coverage has now fallen for two consecutive rounds while the plate wants more.
  * speck_pct_single_px 36.4 -> 33.1 vs 24.6. Still a third single-pixel.
  What DID move is real and I will not under-report it: flesh R closed 33% of the
  gap (131.0 -> 150.6 of a 190.3 target), flesh_GR closed 26% (0.4409 -> 0.4184 of
  0.3505), and speck_area_p95_over_median 16.4 -> 11.0 against the plate's 9.0 is
  the size-distribution fix landing almost exactly. Frozen `clip` on the same
  frame agrees: mask_px 10305 -> 10723, mean_rgb [105.7,61.5,32.1] ->
  [115.0,57.4,30.5], GR_ratio 0.5815 -> 0.4995, and pct_R_ge_255 2.319 -> 1.781,
  i.e. redder AND less clipped. `clip` on 08-citrus-caps: mask_px 5063 -> 4791,
  mean_rgb [72.8,36.7,5.7] -> [79.7,43.1,9.0].
  So round 8 bought BRIGHTNESS and SIZE-SPREAD, not RESOLVED FIBRE. Looking at the
  6x crop of the frozen foam window beside the same window on the scale-matched
  plate settles it: the plate is a chaotic isotropic network of pale many-pixel
  chunks with dark interstices; ours is a smooth pink field with a faint radial
  starburst converging on the exact cap centre -- still radially symmetric, which
  REFERENCE_BAR lists as an auto-fail.

(2) THE APPENDAGE MASK: YES, IMPLEMENTED, AND IT READS. Credit where due.
  species.js:1771 `appendage()` now consumes geometry.js's uv.y mask --
  wood = ss(1.680,1.755,y), leafy = ss(1.020,1.120,y)*(1-wood) -- and geometry.js
  moved its foliage band top 1.70 -> 1.66 in the same round so the two bands do
  not overlap. This is the r7 cross-file finding closed on BOTH sides, and it is
  visible: 09-combo+50ms strawberry calyx sepals were body-red in r7 and are dark
  green in r8; 01-whole-watermelon's stem spur was skin-green in r7 and is a pale
  woody stub in r8. It survives portrait.
  Not fully paid for, though: the melon stem spur is a flat neutral-grey slab with
  no grain and no broken end -- it reads as grey card, not wood -- and the
  pineapple crown went from r7's gold feather-duster to r8's PALE STRAW
  feather-duster. plate-01's crown is grey-green sword leaves with dark spines;
  the A_TIP dry-straw term is winning over A_FOL along most of the blade, so the
  named 'gold feather-duster' tell is recoloured, not removed.

  Portrait's cut face sits at R 96.3 against plate-01's 190.3 -- HALF -- and its
  GR moved away from the plate. The 8x crop confirms it by eye: a flat, even,
  matte salmon disc with black seed dashes stamped on and literally zero internal
  structure. That is the r6 verdict's sentence, unedited, on the config we ship.
  MECHANISM, from the files: `fleshCells` (species.js ~1088) returns
  `bun: crest.mul(w)` and `grv: ss(...).mul(wmax)` where w = pxFade(c, 3.4), and
  its own header records w = 0.70 for the coarse octave and 0.00 for the fine one
  at the 640x360 review frame. pxFade = ss(1/3.4, 0.55/3.4, fw) = ss(0.2941,
  0.1618, fw); inverting the documented 0.70 gives fw = 0.2165 at review. The
  measured portrait face is 0.745x linear (foam ellipse a 45.92 -> 34.21), so
  fw = 0.290, which is past the 0.2941 edge: w falls to ~0.003. bun -> 0, grv -> 0
  (gated by the same wmax), the relief term `fb7.bun.mul(1.20)` -> 0, and rough's
  `-fc.bun*0.14 +fc.grv*0.10` -> 0. Round 6's anti-aliasing guard and round 8's
  brightness payload are the SAME quantity, and they cancel exactly where it
  matters. Each file is correct alone: pxFade's docstring even claims it is
  'automatically correct in portrait', and it is -- for aliasing. It was never
  told the face's MEAN was moved inside the field it kills.

STILL vs MOTION -- what is left. The appendages, the seed embedding, the pith
  collar and the rind layering would all survive motion now. The one thing that
  fails in a still and would not fail in motion is the cut face: a flat matte
  disc of one value is invisible under 120 Hz motion blur and a juice sheet, and
  unmissable frozen. It is also the largest object in every cut frame. Blind, the
  portrait pair is not close -- the flat pink disc is the instant tell.
fix: src/fruit/species.js, `fleshCells` return block (~line 1108): stop multiplying the mesh by its own resolution guard and start CROSS-FADING IT TO ITS AREA MEAN. Change `bun: crest.mul(u.detail.mul(0.26).add(0.74)).clamp(0.0,1.0)` to `bun: mix(float(BUN_MEAN), crest, wmax).mul(u.detail.mul(0.26).add(0.74)).clamp(0.0,1.0)` and `grv: ss(0.52,0.10,prox).mul(wmax)` to `grv: mix(float(GRV_MEAN), ss(0.52,0.10,prox), wmax)`, with BUN_MEAN and GRV_MEAN the measured area means of the two fields at full weight -- the file's own rough() comment already states them as ~0.22 chunk and ~0.30 groove, so BUN_MEAN=0.22, GRV_MEAN=0.30 to start, then solve against the frozen probe. This keeps round 6's rule EXACTLY (no sub-pixel spatial variance survives to alias; the field goes constant, not absent) while keeping the albedo, the 1.20 relief and the roughness redistribution that carry the round-8 brightness -- so portrait inherits desktop's flesh_mean_rgb R instead of 13% of its gain. VERIFY IT ON PORTRAIT, NOT DESKTOP: the acceptance number is `foam shots/r8-iphone/05-cut+500ms.png win=262:352:88:160` flesh_mean_rgb R 96.3 -> >=140 with flesh_GR 0.506 -> <=0.45, and frozen `clip` on the same frame GR_ratio 0.6664 -> <=0.58, with the desktop `foam` row not regressing. Do NOT chase speck_median_area 2.0 -> 4.0 in the same change -- that is the next round's work and it needs a bigger characteristic crest, not a brighter one. And do not touch the appendage block at 1771-1905; it is the one thing on this axis that is now correct.
